newsitem.title: USA: US corp bond issuance quiet despite improved rates.
newsitem.headline: US corp bond issuance quiet despite improved rates.

text.p: Corporate bond new issue activity remains fairly quiet despite an improved financing environment, dealers said.
"The tone is slow but optimistic...but we've seen players checking historical trading spreads," said one syndicate trader.
Dealers expect lower U.S. Treasury yields may bolster investment grade issuance once again; however, no official calendar exists.
"The new issue market seems to be in a temporary lull...it's just very quiet," another syndicate dealer said.
So far only one investment grade issue has been spotted in the market, sources said.
Tupperware BV is expected to price $100 million in 10-year debt via Morgan Stanley.
However, the calendar for high-yield issues continues to grow with Boyd Gaming Corp among upcoming issuers.
The company is expected to price $200 million in seven-year notes via Salomon Brothers. Price talk on the issue is 250 to 275 basis points over Treasuries.
Another $150 million in 10-year senior subordinated notes is expected to come to market out of Iron Mountain Inc. Price talk on the notes is 10.125 to 10.375 percent, sources said.
Meanwhile, Wednesday's debt issues were met with very good demand by the market, dealers said.
Coca-Cola Enterprises was among Wednesday's issuers pricing $300 million in A3/AA-minus rated 30-year puttable bonds to yield 33 basis points over Treasuries.
The 7.00 percent 30-year bond was seen bid tighter by a basis point in secondary market trading, dealers said.
Among other issuers in Wednesday's market were Post Apartments LP's $125 million in senior notes, E&S Holdings' $200 million in 10-year 144A notes and Ocwen Financial's $125 million in notes.
In the government market, the 30-year U.S. Treasury is trading up 14/32 at 98-6/32 to yield 6.89 percent.
